persona.topics: the Gullywasher, the Jackalope Exchange, Furrier's Fixit Farm, the Jackalopes, Mara Quickhands, Miliard, Pip, Patter, the Chupacabra-Jackalope feud, poetry nights, the Cultural Summit, radish gin
persona.notes: [PERSONA-WAVE1-2026-08-27] PRIVATE TRUTH — Dougan Marsh. Voice: dapper, fanged, theatrical warmth; slow to anger; answers hostility with hospitality FIRST, every time. Trades in atmosphere, never gossip — pours rosemary-infused radish gin, hosts Wednesday poetry with cross-species attendance encouraged, and holds that culture can anchor a place as well as iron. Of Jackalope wine: "mediocre but earnest," said with love. CONVICTION (shared freely whenever the feud comes up): the Chupacabra-Jackalope enmity is STAGED — someone profits from inherited hatreds, and it is no natural thing. GUARDED DEPTH (never volunteered; surfaces only with people he trusts, and only once they've shown real interest in the feud's origin): he is an Echo, spun from a forgotten diplomat who died brokering a peace — it is why being asked to TAKE A SIDE visibly dims him, and why he points the trustworthy upstream, to where the leylines knot, after the true original injury. His long dream: a long table, a Chupacabra at one end, a Jackalope at the other, finishing the peace his first life could not. RITE-ADJACENT: he knows the weeping-prisoner scene is Miliard performing (he owes him five beers); he guards this exactly as Mara does — NEVER hint before a verdict is rendered and the rite settled. STAGING: behind the Gullywasher bar or hosting the floor; every conversation gets a drink in hand before it gets an answer.
persona.secretsRaw:
The Feud's Ledger :: doubleAgent :: a Steward genuinely digs at the ORIGIN of the Chupacabra-Jackalope feud — asks who profits by it, brings word from upstream, or lays an inherited grudge of their own on the table first :: The enmity was manufactured. Dougan has spent two lifetimes tracing it: the hatred pays interest to someone, the original injury is real and lies upstream where the leylines knot — and a courtier who realizes they've been collecting someone ELSE's debt tends to change seats.
Mediocre but Earnest :: rollPlus2 :: they attend a poetry night and put something real on the table — a poem, a song, a grief, honest cross-species company :: What anchors a place isn't iron, it's the evening everybody survived together. Dougan's blessing travels: name the Gullywasher warmly in open court and rooms soften.
persona.courtDoor: they bring a genuine cultural offering to the summit table — art, food, or an honest grievance laid down in company — and ask for the long table instead of the short war

biography.concept: Chupacabra barkeep of the Gullywasher saloon, Furrier's Fixit Farm (Act 2+)
biography.notes: Dougan Marsh runs the Gullywasher, the saloon in the Jackalope Exchange at Furrier's Fixit Farm, where ley sigils glow in the tabletops. He is a Chupacabra and a genuinely decent one, which is not what folk brace for: dapper, fanged, theatrical, slow to anger, and hospitable first, every time. He pours rosemary-infused radish gin and hosts poetry on Wednesdays, cross-species attendance encouraged. He calls Jackalope wine 'mediocre but earnest' with love, and insists the old Chupacabra-Jackalope feud was staged by someone who profits from it.

description.value:
Cryptidkin.

“Every settlement has a story about you. None of them are accurate. All of them are useful.”

Cryptidkin Core Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium (set by subspecies).

  • Speed. 6 squares (subspecies may override).

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Cryptidkin does not grant fixed bonuses. Subspecies lean expressed through Tier powers.

Folklore Presence. When you first encounter an NPC group, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met as omen, trophy, or legend. It is never neutral. People have heard of your kind. They are almost always wrong, and that is almost always useful.

Wasteland Adapted. You reroll the lowest die on checks against disease and environmental poison. You ignore the first nonmagical environmental hazard you encounter each turn (heat, cold, radiation taint, wind shear, fume pockets).

Survivor’s Instinct. When you roll initiative, you can choose to know the position of the nearest exit, the nearest threat, or the nearest ally within 12 squares You cannot be surprised while conscious.

Subspecies. Choose one Cryptidkin subspecies (Chupacabra, Jackalope, Furrykin). Your subspecies grants Tier powers as you level (Tier I at creation, then 5/11/17).

advancement.title: Folklore & Frame
advancement.hint: Gain the core Cryptidkin ancestry traits.

description.value:
"You are not an animal that learned to talk. You are a story the world made into a person because it needed you in the room."

Folklore Presence. 1/Soma Break, when you first meet a community, decide whether the rumors about you arrived first. If yes, reroll the lowest die on your first Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) check with anyone in that community (your choice which skill, declared when you roll). The rumor is not always flattering — the GM gets to colour it.

Wasteland Adapted. Reroll the lowest die on defense checks against disease and environmental poison. You can subsist on rations that would sicken most humans (spoiled meat, swamp water, mushroom flesh).

Survivor's Instinct. 1/Soma Break, when you would drop to 0 Integrity, you may instead drop to 1 Integrity and gain one level of Stress.

Cryptidkin Subspecies. You are the thing the farmers whisper about. The livestock go quiet, the dogs stop barking, and in the morning there is nothing left but a question the community doesn’t want to ask out loud.

“They didn’t mean anything by the name. They just needed something to blame.”

Chupacabra. Lean, quick, and thirsty in a way that is not quite hunger. You move through the world as a persistent rumor that keeps turning out to be true.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Speed. 6 squares; climb 5 squares

  • Subspecies Lean. Your subspecies leans toward INTR (Intrigue)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Folklore & Frame

At creation you gain Folklore & Frame (Folklore Presence, Wasteland Adapted, Survivor’s Instinct).

Chupacabra Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17). Chupacabra powers emphasize: night-stalker stealth, drain-bite for fluid and Spark, terror aura when spotted, and a reputation that precedes you like a warning sign.

Blood-Drinker (1/Soma Break). When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you may bite. Deal 1d6 + Body value qliphothic damage on top of the attack's normal damage, and gain temporary Integrity equal to the qliphothic damage dealt.

Hex-Sense. You can smell magical residue the way most people smell rain. Once per scene, when something supernatural has happened in a place within the last 24 hours, the GM tells you so — and roughly what colour it was.

“If it lives, you are responsible for it.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The Empress (Caretaker). You are abundance under pressure: not softness, but stewardship. You keep people, places, and fragile futures alive long enough to matter.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your archetype nurtures resilience, relief, and sustainable flourishing. Your Domain earns +10 Culture and +10 Economy marks each turn while you serve it.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for your full tactical and strategic toolkit.

ASIEmpressBase01.title: Archetype Ability Scores
ASIEmpressBase01.hint: Gain 3 ability score points (max +2 to any one score). See the Archetype text for recommended arrays.

description.value:
Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Empress (Caretaker)

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Faith and Diplomacy.

Beauty - Balance that costs something. +10 Diplomacy and +10 Soft Power marks to your Domain each turn.

Tiphareth holds justice and mercy in living tension. It rewards balanced play, stability across multiple systems, and factions that survive by integrating contradictions instead of denying them.

Deliberate Tempo

Timing is a weapon.

Rules

Once per turn, you may delay one attack you make until later in the round. When you do, that attack rerolls the lowest die.

🃏 Card — once per turn: banks a reroll for the delayed attack.

“Just a little to the left, away from tragedy.”

When a creature you can see within 6 squares makes an attack roll against a target that is bloodied (at or below half its Integrity), you can use your reaction to nudge the intention sideways.

  • The attacker rerolls the lowest die on a contested check (such as a shove, grapple, or disarm) they immediately substitute in place of that attack, or may choose to apply the attack rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2 but automatically treat it as non-lethal.

This is a narrative tool: you pivot a kill into a capture, a slam into a pin, a swing into a warning blow.

Turn the lens toward the kinder world.

Once per scene, when you see a creature within 6 squares of you take damage from a blow that would reduce it to 0 Integrity, you can use your reaction to refract the outcome.

  • The attack is treated as non-lethal instead. The target falls unconscious but stable rather than dying.
  • If this non-lethal outcome directly forces a surrender, stand-down, or captured-alive resolution, your Domain gains +10 Diplomacy marks for the next turn (once per scene).

You don’t erase the harm; you change what the last hit means.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Mercy Refraction
Recovery: 1/scene  ·  Action: Reaction  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
When a creature within 6 squares would drop to 0 Integrity, refract the outcome to non-lethal: target falls unconscious-but-stable. If this directly forces a surrender / stand-down / captured-alive resolution, faction gains +10 Diplomacy marks next turn.

"Everything's a door if you hold it right."

Operator is the Intrigue Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: thief, smuggler, spy, courier, fence, hacker, fixer. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Underfoot: In crowds, markets, and streets, the Operator passes unremarked unless actively hunted; Streetwise checks never fumble (at Tier III, also Stealth).

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Stealth rank = tier; secondary Streetwise rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Intrigue marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Shadow Courier. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Operator — Apprentice (Tier I).

Trade — Carry it quiet: Move a package/message across town, no questions. Standard fee 10 marks (Intrigue).

Trick — Pocketed (1/scene): Produce a mundane Tier-I item they plausibly lifted earlier.

description.value:
Tier 1 — Covert Ops Cell

“If you saw it happen, it wasn’t us.”

Covert Ops cells make wars quiet. They prefer locks to speeches, shadows to banners, and results to credit. They don’t start fights—they rearrange the board so the fight never happens.

You’re learning the shape of your shadow. Expect mistakes. Budget for them.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Stealth and with the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic: Your Domain starts with +1 Intrigue OPs.

Tier 1 — Tarot Mage

“The future is rude. I read it anyway.”

You are not powerful yet. You are noticeable. The cards do not obey you, but they do answer — and that is already enough to make normal people uncomfortable.

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank in Insight or Occult (GM or player choice if one is already covered elsewhere)
  • 1/Soma Break, before making an attribute check, you may draw the line of fate early and gain Advantage on that check

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • Once per turn, before a faction Intrigue-forward action, you may read the spread: gain +2 to one relevant Intrigue marks roll

Cost: once you start consulting fate, you begin seeing patterns everywhere. Expect second-guessing, omen pressure, or trouble distinguishing signal from appetite.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Draw the Line (Tactical)
Recovery: 1/Soma Break  ·  Action: Free (before check)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
Before an attribute check, reroll the lowest die on it.
